subject: Proposal: percentile envelope SLOs with blackout-aware measurement for Hosted API
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@gridly.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Latency commitments for our streaming product

David —

Thanks for the sync last week. As we move toward production we need clearer commitments on tail latency for the Hosted API: our UX team has seen spikes that make live captions stutter, and legal wants SLO language we can include in our procurement doc. Two specific asks:

1) Can Redwood commit to numerical p50 / p95 targets measured in a way that aligns to our real-time SLAs? We prefer something that preserves hourly behavior rather than a monthly aggregate.
2) How will scheduled maintenance, cloud provider incidents, and short network flaps be treated? We need predictable carveouts or blackout definitions.

If useful, we can share a sample SLA paragraph. Goal is to get to a handshake on numbers and measurement so procurement can draft the PO.

Tom
Tom Hayes
Head of Platform
Gridly

--
Attachment: example_sla_paragraph.txt (text)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@gridly.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-20T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Latency commitments for our streaming product

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. Below is a draft approach we think balances predictability with operational reality; attaching a short diff that highlights the measurement and blackout language. Summary:

- Measurement: define p50 and p95 as a 60-minute moving envelope computed from 5-minute sliding percentiles (i.e., compute percentiles per 5-min slice, then the SLO is the max percentile observed across the prior 12 slices). This keeps the SLO responsive to hourly spikes while avoiding minute-level noise.
- Numeric targets (proposal): p50 <= 120 ms, p95 <= 1.2 s for typical text-generation requests (tokens<=256). We can provide separate bands for long-seq and embeddings.
- Blackouts/carveouts: scheduled maintenance will be excluded if announced >=48 hours and documented in our status page with a start/end window. Unscheduled provider network incidents are eligible for a one-time transient carveout (<=2 hours per quarter) with post-incident evidence (traces + provider incident id). Regional failovers: 15-minute regional failover grace per event, up to 1 hour per month aggregated.
- Evidence & reporting: we publish hourly percentile telemetry to a shared dashboard for the life of the contract and will provide a quarterly evidence bundle for any claimed carveouts.

I've attached SLO_Diff_v1.pdf with the draft language. Happy to take edits; if you like this shape, we can convert to contractual wording.

Next steps: if this aligns, propose a short call tomorrow to walk the procurement team through the measurement method.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0123

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-20T13:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Latency commitments for our streaming product — negotiation points

Looping you in — Tom pushed for hourly-aligned SLOs (not monthly aggregates). My draft proposes the 60-minute moving envelope computed from 5-min slices; numeric asks above. A few points I want advice on before we send a commit:

- Can we legally accept the 15-minute regional failover grace? I worry about cumulative exposure if Gridly is high-volume.
- Should we reduce the p95 target to 1.0s to be conservative for live UX, or keep 1.2s and offer credits/mitigation?
- For the transient carveout, do we want to cap per incident or per quarter? I suggested <=2 hours per quarter.

Suggested commercial mitigations: guaranteed canary fallback to a smaller context model (documented QoS difference) and a bill credit for any verified SLO breach >1 hour in a month.

Thoughts quickly pls — procurement wants a clean paragraph for the PO by end of the week.

Thanks,
David

> On Jun 20, 2026, at 11:30 AM, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original draft to customer attached)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-20T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency commitments for our streaming product — negotiation points

David / Naomi —

High level: I like the 60-minute envelope approach; it's simple to explain. A few edits to the mechanics I recommend before we lock numbers:

- Change wording from "max percentile observed across the prior 12 slices" to "the 60-minute envelope equal to the 95th percentile of 5-minute percentile samples" — this reads better for legal.
- Keep p95 target at 1.2s for the initial term; offer a roadmap to 1.0s after a 60-day opt-in performance run (we can instrument and show stability). That gives Gridly a path without immediate exposure.
- For carveouts: keep per-quarter cap at 2 hours but require that consecutive incidents be aggregated and billed as one carveout if within the same 48-hour outage window. This prevents gaming.
- Add a clause: "Regional failovers exceeding the 15-minute grace will be considered operational incidents and eligible for remediation credits."

On the mitigation side, instead of an automatic credit for >1 hour breach, propose a remediation playbook first (automated fallback, priority support), then credits if remediation fails to bring service within SLO for more than 4 hours in a rolling 30-day window.

I'll draft the legal-friendly paragraph and post to the shared doc. Naomi — can you confirm we have telemetry hooks to produce the hourly dashboard slices and that the engineering team is ok with the 5-min percentile granularity?

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Contracts

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-21T09:05:00Z
Subject: Final proposal: percentile envelope SLO + blackout language (GMT)

Tom —

Thanks for the patience — attached is a cleaned-up proposal that incorporates Gridly's ask for hourly-aligned measurement and the changes Lauren suggested. Key points:

- Measurement: p50/p95 defined using a 60-minute percentile envelope built from 5-minute percentile samples (legal paragraph updated for clarity).
- Targets: p50 <= 120 ms; p95 <= 1.2 s for standard-generation requests (tokens <=256). We include an optional 60-day performance ramp to target p95 <= 1.0 s (mutually agreeable, opt-in).
- Blackouts: scheduled maintenance excluded with >=48-hour notice; transient provider/network incidents eligible for a carveout up to 2 hours per quarter; regional failover 15-minute grace with aggregation rules.
- Evidence: hourly telemetry available on shared dashboard + quarterly evidence bundle for carveouts.
- Remedies: remediation-first playbook, with credits only if remediation fails to restore SLO for >4 hours in a rolling 30-day window.

I've attached SLO_Diff_v2.pdf which highlights the final wording and posted the full clause here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cGRIDLY-SLO-PROPOSAL. If this reflects Gridly's needs, please let me know and I will ask legal to prep an addendum for signature.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Wednesday to walk procurement through measurement and evidence. Are you available 10:00–10:30 PT?

Best,
